- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.7) — model tends to overshoot in bullish periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (especially <0.3) — model fails to capture bearish momentum.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially after sharp spikes or drops.
- After a price spike, model often overcorrects and forecasts a sharp drop — adjust downward by 5–10% of peak value if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs/lows; reduce forecast volatility if sentiment is stable or mildly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model overestimates early in the period when sentiment is rising — cap forecast at 1.5–2x recent high if sentiment >0.6.
- If sentiment is consistently low (e.g., <0.2 for 3+ days), reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in recovery.
